Lesson 4 of 10 in *Vital, step by step*: everything you need to feel at home in the real Vital plug-in. Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what attack, decay, sustain and release mean.
2. Shape the loudness with Envelope 1: a swell and a pluck.
3. Move the filter and the wave frame with Envelope 2.
4. Use Envelope 3 through the matrix.
5. Find the real Vital's six envelopes.
:::

## What an envelope is

- An **envelope** is a shape over time that starts when you press a key and ends after you let go. It moves something for you: the loudness, the cutoff, the wave frame.
- It has four parts, written **ADSR**:
  - **Attack**: how long it takes to rise when you press the key.
  - **Decay**: how long it takes to fall to the sustain level.
  - **Sustain**: the level it holds while the key stays down (a level, not a time).
  - **Release**: how long it takes to fade after you let go.

## Times in Vital

- Vital's attack, decay and release knobs run from 0 to about 2.378 (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp). They are not seconds: this page reads the knob value to the power 4 as seconds (1.0 = 1 s, 2.378 = 32 s), a reading of the code (unverified).
- So small moves near 0 are tiny times, and the same move near the top is many seconds.

## Which envelope does what

- On this page **Envelope 1** always shapes the loudness. In the real Vital, Envelope 1 controls the loudness at the start too, but that is not stated in the files read (unverified).
- **Envelope 2** has two fixed routes here: **→ cutoff** and **→ frame** (the small knobs under it).
- **Envelope 3** is on the MATRIX tab and does nothing until a matrix slot uses it.

## Step by step

Each step loads a starting patch made on this page (not one of Vital's presets) and plays it. Listen for the one thing it names, then turn the knob it names.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;e1A&quot;:0.9,&quot;e1R&quot;:1.0}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A slow swell.</b> Envelope 1 <b>ATTACK</b> 0.9 (about 0.7 s) and <b>RELEASE</b> 1.0. Listen: each note fades in and rings on after it ends. Turn ATTACK down to 0 for a sharp start.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;e1A&quot;:0,&quot;e1D&quot;:0.5,&quot;e1S&quot;:0,&quot;e1R&quot;:0.3}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A pluck.</b> <b>SUSTAIN</b> 0 %, <b>DECAY</b> 0.5, <b>ATTACK</b> 0. Each note starts loud and dies away even while the key is held, like a plucked string. Raise DECAY to 0.9 for a longer ring.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;e1D&quot;:0.7,&quot;e1S&quot;:40}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Decay to a sustain.</b> <b>DECAY</b> 0.7, <b>SUSTAIN</b> 40 %. Hold a key: it starts loud, then settles to a quieter level and stays. Move SUSTAIN up and down while holding a key.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;cut&quot;:50,&quot;res&quot;:35,&quot;e2Cut&quot;:36,&quot;e2A&quot;:0,&quot;e2D&quot;:0.6,&quot;e2S&quot;:0,&quot;e2R&quot;:0.3}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Envelope 2 on the cutoff.</b> The filter is nearly closed (cutoff 50), and <b>Env 2 → cutoff</b> at +36 opens it at the start of each note: a "blip". Make Envelope 2's DECAY longer (0.9) for a slower "wow".</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-morph" data-page="voice"><p><b>Envelope 2 on the wave frame.</b> <b>Env 2 → frame</b> at 256 moves OSC 1 from sine to saw on every note: brighter as the note goes on, with no filter at all. Make Envelope 2's ATTACK shorter and listen again.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;m1s&quot;:&quot;Env 3&quot;,&quot;m1d&quot;:&quot;Osc 1 pitch&quot;,&quot;m1a&quot;:6,&quot;e3A&quot;:0,&quot;e3D&quot;:0.45,&quot;e3S&quot;:0,&quot;e3R&quot;:0.3}" data-page="matrix"><p><b>Envelope 3 through the matrix.</b> Slot 1: <b>Env 3 → Osc 1 pitch</b>, 6 %. Envelope 3 has no sustain and a short decay, so each note starts a little high and drops: a "zap". Turn Envelope 3's DECAY up on the MATRIX tab for a slower drop.</p></div>
```

## In the real Vital

What is different in the plug-in and exactly where to find it. Every line names the file of Vital's source code (github.com/mtytel/vital) it was read from; "(unverified)" means it was not confirmed.

- **Six envelopes:** ENVELOPE 1 to 6, one shown at a time; click the numbered buttons on the left of the envelope area to switch (Vital source, synth_constants.h; modulation_interface.cpp).
- **Six knobs, not four:** **DELAY**, ATTACK, **HOLD**, DECAY, SUSTAIN, RELEASE (Vital source, envelope_section.cpp). DELAY waits before the attack starts; HOLD keeps the top level for a while before the decay.
- **Curves:** attack, decay and release can each be bent into a curve, not only a straight line (Vital source, envelope_section.cpp).
- **Drag the picture:** drag the points of the envelope graph left and right for times and the sustain point up and down for the level; drag a curve handle up or down to bend it, double-click it to straighten it; the mouse wheel zooms (Vital source, envelope_editor.cpp).
- **Starting values:** attack 0.1495, decay 1.0, sustain 100 %, release 0.5476 on the knob's own scale (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp). The seconds those mean are not in the notes (unverified).
- **Any envelope, anywhere:** in the real Vital you drag the **ENV 2** button (or any ENV button) onto any knob (lesson 5). This page's fixed *→ cutoff* and *→ frame* knobs stand in for that.

## Try it in the real Vital

Open Vital in your DAW (see [Meet Vital](intro-vital.qmd) to install it) and do these in order.

- [ ] Initialize the preset. Click ENVELOPE 1 and drag its ATTACK point to the right. Play: the sound fades in.
- [ ] Drag the sustain point down to the bottom for a pluck.
- [ ] Bend the decay curve by dragging its handle; double-click the handle to straighten it.
- [ ] Click ENV 2 and look at its knobs: DELAY, ATTACK, HOLD, DECAY, SUSTAIN, RELEASE.
- [ ] Lesson 5 shows how to drag ENV 2 onto the cutoff.

<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A plucked sound has…</b></p><ul><li>Short attack, no sustain</li><li>Long attack, full sustain</li><li>No release at all</li><li>Only release</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Envelope 2 → cutoff makes each note…</b></p><ul><li>Open the filter and close it again</li><li>Louder for ever</li><li>Change wavetable</li><li>Play an octave up</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 4.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How many envelopes does the real Vital have?</b></p><ul><li>6</li><li>2</li><li>3</li><li>64</li></ul><p class="ik-why">kNumEnvelopes = 6 (synth_constants.h).</p></div>
